The successful completion of the Perinatal Education Programme has been found to not directly impact obstetric practice, despite improvements in knowledge among midwives. The programme's effectiveness is highlighted by its inability to alter obstetric practice in response to these changes.

While the programme does lead to improved knowledge among midwives, it is essential to note that this improvement in knowledge does not necessarily translate into better obstetric practices. Obstetric practice involves a complex interplay of factors, including clinical judgment, decision-making, and collaboration with healthcare teams.

In other words, while having a better understanding of the obstetric manual may help midwives provide more informed care, it is crucial to recognize that other factors, such as clinical experience, patient preferences, and socioeconomic considerations, also play a significant role in shaping obstetric practice.
